skill.name: zentao-tour
skill.description: Guides users through ZenTao and zentao-cli onboarding by role, using conversational tours for product, project, test, developer, and executive workflows.
skill.summary: Run role-based ZenTao onboarding tours with zentao-cli.
skill.author: easysoft

security_audit.summary: Most high-severity static alerts are false positives from Markdown links, Chinese prose, and documentation paths. The confirmed risks are the intended zentao-cli command flows that can read, create, update, and delete ZenTao records. No evidence of prompt injection or encoded payloads was found.

remediation.issue: CLI write operations can affect real ZenTao data.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a sandbox workspace by default and clearly label any production write action before running commands.

remediation.issue: Login guidance uses password arguments in shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer token-based or interactive login and warn users not to paste passwords into shared chat logs.

remediation.issue: Cleanup guidance uses destructive delete commands with --yes.
remediation.suggestion: Track records created during the tour and show a clear deletion list before cleanup.

remediation.issue: MCP examples include configuration fields for server URLs and tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify server URLs and avoid committing real tokens in MCP configuration files.

semantic_findings.title: Accidental ZenTao Data Mutation During Tour
semantic_findings.description: The tour intentionally guides create, update, status transition, and delete actions in a connected ZenTao environment. The casual onboarding tone can cause unintended changes if used against production data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple role files and the main skill explicitly direct record creation, updates, state transitions, and deletion. The instructions require consent, so this is operational risk rather than clear malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Command-Line Credential Exposure in Login Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The setup guidance shows zentao login with a password parameter and says credentials are cached under the user config directory. Password arguments can appear in shell history, process listings, or chat transcripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The login command examples directly include a password flag, and the overview describes credential caching. This is common CLI guidance but creates a concrete secret exposure risk.

content.value_statement: New ZenTao users often struggle to connect roles, objects, and command-line actions. This skill guides a role-based tour through real ZenTao workflows.
actual_capabilities: Checks the active ZenTao CLI profile before starting the tour.
Routes users to product manager, project manager, tester, developer, or executive walkthroughs.
Explains ZenTao objects such as products, stories, plans, tasks, bugs, and test cases.
Provides conversational prompts for creating and updating demo ZenTao records.
Shows read-only executive views for project, product, release, feedback, and ticket data.
Points users to zentao-cli installation, login, and MCP configuration guidance.
limitations: Requires zentao-cli and access to a reachable ZenTao instance.
May create, update, or delete records when the user approves write actions.
Does not verify whether the connected ZenTao environment is safe for demo data.
Role walkthroughs are guided examples, not complete ZenTao administration training.

use_cases.title: Onboard Product Managers
use_cases.description: Guide a product manager from a product idea to requirements and a first product plan.

use_cases.title: Teach Project Flow
use_cases.description: Help a project manager create a project, open a sprint, assign tasks, and review status changes.

use_cases.title: Practice Testing Workflows
use_cases.description: Walk a tester from a requirement to test cases, a test task, a bug, and closure.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Product Tour
prompt_templates.prompt: Take me on a ZenTao tour as a product manager. Help me create a demo product and explain each object.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a project manager walkthrough. Use existing products, create a sprint, and show task status flow after asking first.

prompt_templates.title: Run a QA Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide my ZenTao testing workflow from requirement to test case, test task, bug report, resolution, and closure.

prompt_templates.title: Review Executive Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the executive view to summarize project pace, product health, releases, feedback, and the next area to inspect.

output_examples.input: I want to try the product manager path.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for a product idea, helps name it, records a few requirements, and groups selected items into a first plan.

output_examples.input: Show me what a manager can see without changing data.
output_examples.output: The skill lists active projects, explains schedule and progress signals, and summarizes product health from requirements and bugs.

output_examples.input: I want to clean up demo data.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews created records, asks for confirmation before each deletion, and runs cleanup only after approval.

best_practices: Use a sandbox ZenTao workspace when trying write flows.
Confirm each create, update, delete, or status transition before running it.
Track IDs created during a tour so cleanup is accurate.
anti_patterns: Running the tour against production data without a rollback plan.
Skipping role selection and mixing unrelated workflows in one session.
Pasting real passwords or tokens into shared chat logs.

faq.question: Does this skill require zentao-cli?
faq.answer: Yes. The walkthrough depends on zentao-cli for profile checks and ZenTao actions.

faq.question: Can this skill change my ZenTao data?
faq.answer: Yes. Product, project, task, bug, and cleanup flows can write data after user approval.

faq.question: Which roles does the tour support?
faq.answer: It supports product manager, project manager, tester, developer, executive, and a flexible browse mode.

faq.question: Can I use it in read-only mode?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for the executive view or tell the assistant to avoid write actions.

faq.question: Does it install ZenTao itself?
faq.answer: No. It gives zentao-cli setup guidance and expects access to an existing ZenTao server.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production data?
faq.answer: Use a sandbox when possible. Production use needs careful confirmations and a clear cleanup plan.
